name: ROGII silver-medal structural-coordinate tracker (EdidiongA / Edidiong-Abasi Anwanane): u = TVT + Z, second-order (u, dip) banded trellis, windowed GR emissions against a merged typewell/pseudo-typewell reference, inverse-variance branch fusion with a spatial field, deployment-side dose calibration
venue_link: Kaggle ROGII - Wellbore Geology Prediction (241/6,125, silver, top 4%); GitHub https://github.com/EdidiongA/wellbore-tvt-prediction ; preprint 'Blind-Zone TVT Prediction in Horizontal Wells: An Information-Ceiling Study with Deployment-Side Dose Calibration' (PDF in repo papers/rogii_preprint_Anwanane.pdf, 29 pages; arXiv link announced as forthcoming); author site https://edidionga.github.io/
code_availability: Public, MIT license: tracker notebooks (final base model/rogii_tvt_tracker_v22.ipynb), neural line (1D U-Net, BiGRU with 5-fold OOF), postprocessing v25-v58 one mechanism per file, diagnostics L1-L8, full campaign ledger docs/campaign_log.md. Written for the Kaggle CPU offline environment; competition data not redistributed.
evidence_level: Competition writeup plus public code plus a self-published (not peer-reviewed) preprint with a full submission ledger (public and some private scores per version) and leave-one-well-out measurements.
extreme_summary: Reparameterise the target as the smooth structural coordinate u = TVT + Z and track (u, dip) with a second-order HMM whose prior makes constant dip free and dip changes expensive. Emissions are clipped |GR - ref(u - Z)| against a typewell blended with the well's own known-zone GR. CPU only, about 4 s per well, private 8.354 (base 8.416). Much weaker than the U-Net line, but built from very different assumptions.
task_definition: Predict TVT at every blind-zone station (median ~4,800 stations, ~74% of the lateral) of a horizontal well from the known-zone TVT prefix, trajectory (X, Y, Z, MD), horizontal GR, and one vertical typewell (GR vs TVT). The method tracks the smooth structural curve u(MD) and recovers TVT = u - Z.
inputs: Horizontal GR; trajectory Z (and X, Y for the spatial field); known-zone TVT_input (prefix labels); typewell GR vs TVT, affine-mapped to horizontal-tool GR units by a trimmed least-squares fit on the known zone; pseudo-typewell = known-zone (TVT, GR) pairs binned over TVT; for the spatial branch, the known-zone u-curves of training/neighbour wells (IDW local gradient fits over X, Y). No offset logs.
target_parameterisation: Structural coordinate u = TVT + Z (stratigraphic position = geology minus wellbore). Paper evidence: replacing true u by its 2,000 ft moving average costs only ~3 ft; an oracle knowing u smoothed at 300 ft scores 0.86 ft; high-passed TVT and Z correlate at -0.74 per well. Explicit dip state (grid steps per 30 ft block, within +-14 steps). Their neural line found the increment u - u_lastknown (drift relative to the anchor) much better than absolute datum-centred u (prototype 22.6 -> 12.65 ft).
output_representation: Discrete posterior over (u, dip) per 30 ft block. Two decodes, Viterbi MAP path and forward-backward posterior mean, ensembled at two positional-prior strengths. Five semi-independent branch paths are fused per station into one point estimate, weighted by the inverse variance of their disagreement.
architecture: (1) Merged reference: the typewell is mapped to tool units and blended with the pseudo-typewell using weight w = n/(n+3) (n = local smoothed known-zone sample count), then EM re-estimates the reference along the pass-1 path. (2) Second-order HMM over 30 ft MD blocks, state (u on a 0.5 ft grid inside a per-well band, dip), with banded transitions vectorised through precomputed gather maps. Coarse-to-fine: a 1 ft scout pass locates the drift tube, the full ensemble runs at 0.5 ft within tube +-150 ft, the final grid is 0.25 ft, and the full band is redone when the path grazes the band edge. (3) Branches: drift-cancelling (windowed mean cancellation between observed GR and reference, targets slow gain drift; weight 0.40), typewell-only (0.28 / 0.15, a hedge against pseudo-reference failure), their combination, the pre-branch ensemble, and a GR-independent spatial structural field (IDW gradient fits of neighbour known-zone u-curves). (4) Inverse-variance fusion per station; the field can take weight up to 0.95 where the branches scatter. (5) Post-processing found by leaderboard dose-response: position-ramped toe damping of far-toe curvature toward the near-blind linear trend (S ~0.13-0.15), high-frequency shrinkage (h = 0.40, window 601), and a global signed cubic drift profile (toe -2.4 ft). (6) Guards fall back to constant continuation on malformed wells, low known-zone GR correlation, or non-finite output.
core_mechanism: The coordinate change turns a jagged 5,000-sample regression into estimating one smooth curve with few effective degrees of freedom, and TVT = u - Z restores every wiggle exactly. On top of that sits a second-order (dip-persistence) prior: steady dip costs nothing and dip changes cost lambda = 300. The author argues that first-order smoothness priors fail here because they penalise real steady drift, which is everywhere, in order to suppress noise. Other load-bearing ideas: using the well's own known-zone GR as a reference (largest classical gain, 11.63 -> 11.20), and using uncertain priors proportionally (inverse-variance pull) instead of snapping to them. The discrete field prior failed on hidden wells (10.200 vs 9.382) even though it won every local holdout.
training_objective: No gradient training. Hand-set costs: clipped absolute GR residual emission, dip-change penalty lambda = 300, a weak positional prior of 0.02 per ft of deviation from constant continuation, plus a zero-prior member weighted 40%. Branch weights and regularisation doses were tuned on a 'corrupted suite' of perturbed training wells and on leaderboard probes. The separate BiGRU line used masked L1 on blind stations only.
decoding: Viterbi (MAP) and forward-backward (posterior mean) decodes averaged at two prior strengths, then inverse-variance fusion of branches, then damping, HF shrinkage and a drift profile.
metric_consistent_decode: [uncertain] Mixed. The posterior-mean part is right for squared error; the Viterbi/MAP part seeks the mode, which can raise RMSE. The preprint calls the metric MAE, which would make a median the right decode, but the 1st and 14th place writeups report RMSE, so the preprint's label may be a mistake.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral (sequence-level HMM over the full blind zone) plus typewell; the spatial branch adds multiple wells jointly through an IDW structural field.
prefix_conditioning: Heavy and closed-form. It uses the anchor at the known/blind boundary (audited at 0.01 ft median error), a per-well band centred on constant continuation, an affine typewell-to-tool GR calibration fitted on the known zone, the pseudo-typewell built from known-zone (TVT, GR) pairs, and the known-zone u-curves that feed the spatial field. Prefix self-calibration (hiding the tail of the known zone to choose configurations) was measured as invalid: the pseudo-blind zone is ~10x shorter and 2.7x easier, and selecting on it cost 0.249 ft.
propose_vs_select: Produces one fused path per well. Internally it proposes (five branches, two decodes) and fuses them by disagreement-weighted averaging, not selection. Cheap enough (CPU) to act as one ensemble member or an input channel for us. The author's own routing test (tracker vs BiGRU) found a cross-fitted routing gain of exactly 0.
physical_constraints: u = TVT + Z identity (exact); locally constant dip (second-order persistence); banded u range; clipped emission for washouts; positional prior toward constant continuation; spatial structural field that assumes locally linear surfaces.
dataset: [uncertain] ROGII Kaggle competition: 773 fully interpreted training wells (~3.78M stations) and about 200 hidden wells scored server-side (public/private split), clustered on multi-well pads. Region: a US unconventional basin (not named). The preprint gives the hidden-well count only approximately.
synthetic_to_real: No synthetic data. Real-to-typewell GR normalisation by a trimmed least-squares affine fit on the known zone, blended with the pseudo-typewell (w = n/(n+3)), with EM refinement of the reference along the first-pass path.
metric_and_performance: Leaderboard ladder: constant continuation 15.88 public; v2 bare (u, dip) tracker 13.196; + merged reference/EM/drift-cancel 11.630; typewell-only branch 11.197; proportional spatial field 9.624; inverse-variance fusion 8.926; sealed base v22 8.913 public / 8.416 private; final v55 8.720 public / 8.354 private (241/6,125). The tracker's honest leave-one-well-out OOF on all 773 wells is 5.507 ft, giving a 3.41 ft train-to-hidden gap. BiGRU line on identical inputs: 6.9-7.1 ft OOF (5 well-grouped folds). Tracker vs BiGRU per-well error correlation 0.171; the best fixed blend (0.10 toward the BiGRU) gains only +0.079 ft. Oracles: perfect routing 0.86 ft, perfect per-well slope removal 0.80 ft, perfect configuration selection 0.56 ft; none could be predicted at inference.
comparability: [uncertain] Weak. Scores are on the Kaggle hidden set (private ~8.35) or 773-well LOWO (5.51), not our 155-well holdout. The 14th place U-Net line scored 6.33 private on the same leaderboard, so this tracker is about 2 ft (roughly 30%) worse than U-Net solutions of our family. Our 4.84 ft local-holdout number compares with their local numbers only after matching protocols. The metric label (MAE in the preprint vs RMSE elsewhere) adds more doubt.
validation_protocol: Leave-one-well-out with the spatial field rebuilt excluding every point of the evaluated well (post-exclusion median nearest-neighbour distance 468 ft); a pad holdout (246 wells in 2,500 ft neighbourhoods); corrupted-well suites; a fitted local-to-leaderboard transfer law. Key warnings: local and hidden orderings inverted repeatedly (v25, best local at 5.459, gave the worst hidden score, 9.302); random holdouts flatter spatial mechanisms because pad-mates remain in the field; the final regularisation doses were fitted to the public leaderboard, which is not fold-safe.
inference_budget: About 4-6 s per well on one CPU core; the whole hidden set in under 40 min; no GPU, no training. Fits any rig or Kaggle budget easily.
repeated_layers: Not handled explicitly. The banded trellis limits hypotheses to a per-well band around constant continuation (a tube found by the scout pass). Clipped GR emissions and the pseudo-typewell (same tool, same well) sharpen matching. Forward-backward keeps several bands alive until the mean decode. The spatial field acts as a GR-independent tie-breaker. It is applied proportionally (inverse variance) instead of as a discrete snap, because the discrete version picked the wrong rung at high confidence on hidden wells.
drift: The main target of the design. The explicit dip state with zero-cost persistence represents steady drift instead of penalising it; the drift-cancelling branch removes slow GR gain drift; a zero-prior member (40%) avoids pulling toward constant continuation. The author showed the residual error is slope-shaped (subtracting each well's fitted drift rate would gain 0.80 ft) but not predictable from any internal observable (OOF Spearman 0.095). A typewell-derived slope correction was the only CI-positive local effect (+0.082 ft) and lost 0.389 ft on the hidden set. The gains that did work were toe damping toward the near-blind linear trend and a global signed cubic drift ramp, both tuned on the leaderboard.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Uses per-station branch disagreement (spread across five paths) as its uncertainty measure and weights by inverse variance. No reliability diagrams or ECE. Error grows along the lateral from ~3.6 ft near the anchor to ~33 ft at the toe. The author notes the field is sometimes wrong with high confidence on hidden wells.
where_to_use: (a) As a structured decode over our per-column posteriors: replace the independent per-column expectation with a second-order (u, dip) forward-backward that uses the ConvNeXt/FastViT column softmax as its emission, and read out the posterior mean. (b) As a cheap CPU ensemble member or extra input channel: render the tracker path and its disagreement spread into the 16-channel cost image, as the 1st place did with PF features. (c) As design rules for the gate/blend: blend proportionally by inverse variance or disagreement, never snap to one choice, and build references from the well's own known zone.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) through the explicit dip state and drift-cancel branch; secondarily band confusion (~51%) through whole-lateral evidence and a disagreement-weighted spatial pull.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already have: the 1st-place recipe calibrates typewell GR from the visible region by TVT binning (equivalent to their pseudo-typewell blend); the Z-shift augmentation keeps TVT + Z invariant, so the network implicitly learns the u identity; TVT is predicted relative to the anchor (their increment finding). What we lack: (1) Any explicit dip/slope state. Our per-column softmax + expectation decode treats columns independently. From the context description, our failed post-hoc forward-backward continuity decode used a first-order smoothness prior, and the preprint gives a concrete reason such priors fail (they tax steady drift). A second-order dip-persistence transition in u-space has not been tried and is the main untested variant. (2) Disagreement-based inverse-variance fusion. Our learned per-point ConvNeXt/AnchorCNN gates failed, while their unlearned weighting by live disagreement was their largest single hidden-set gain. (3) A GR-independent structural-field branch used proportionally. Our XY geo-prior hump picking failed as a discrete pick, which is exactly the failure they documented (discrete field prior 10.200 vs 9.382); the soft, confidence-weighted pull has not been tried. (4) Position-ramped toe damping and HF shrinkage are cheap post-hoc checks for the drift mode, but their doses were tuned on the leaderboard and local LOWO priced them as harmful, so gains may not show on our holdout.
proposed_experiment: E1 (main, CPU-only, ~1 day): add kaggle_1st_place/solution/posterior_dip_decode.py next to posterior_fb_decode.py. Load the dumped posteriors (seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all, results/baseline_check_posterior_all). Per well, map each column's 400-level posterior into u = TVT + Z (shift by the column's Z relative to the anchor). Run forward-backward over state (u, dip), dip in {-K..K} grid steps per column, with u_{t+1} = u_t + dip_t, zero cost for persistence, and dip changes costing lambda (sweep 10, 30, 100, 300). Add a small jump probability for faults. Emission = log(posterior^(1/T)), T in {1, 1.5, 2}. Decode the posterior-mean u, then TVT = u - Z. Controls: the plain expectation decode on the same dumps (FastViT 4.84 / ConvNeXt), plus the old first-order FB decode. Pick lambda/T on training wells; report pooled RMSE on the 155 holdout wells with a paired per-well bootstrap against the +-0.39 ft noise floor, and split the change across wrong_mode / blend / drift buckets with posterior_analysis.py. E2: disagreement-weighted blend, w_i proportional to 1/variance over {ConvNeXt, FastViT, AnchorCNN} per column (no learning), against the fixed-weight pair (4.69). E3: soft XY field pull: add the 1st-place estimate dTVT = a*dX + b*dY - dZ as a Gaussian log-prior term inside E1's emission, with variance set from neighbourhood-quality stats (proportional, not a hump pick). E4 (optional): port the tracker notebook as an extra blend member and check per-well error correlation with ConvNeXt; expect a weight of 0.1 or less.
implementation_effort: Low-medium. E1/E2 are numpy on existing posterior dumps; a banded forward-backward with a few thousand states over 345 columns is cheap. Porting the full tracker with reference EM, branches and field is medium effort (MIT notebooks exist but are written for Kaggle).
gpu_cost: [uncertain] None for E1-E4 (CPU post-processing on existing posterior dumps). The full tracker takes ~4-6 s per well single-core, about 10-15 min for 155 wells. Our own u-space FB decode runtime has not been measured; the estimate is seconds per well.
distillation_compatibility: Compatible. The dip-aware decode runs after the network on its output posteriors, so it applies unchanged to the FastViT student. Dip-decoded posterior marginals could also serve as KD targets (untested).
error_correlation_with_ours: Tracker errors are likely close to independent of ours (in the author's study, tracker vs BiGRU per-well error correlation was 0.171). But the tracker is ~2 ft worse than U-Net solutions, and the author's best blend weight was only 0.10 (+0.079 ft), so as a raw blend member expect little. Its value lies in its structure: using its prior inside our decode, or its disagreement as a confidence signal.
risk: (1) Our failed forward-backward continuity decode suggests the posterior already carries most of the sequential information the network can extract; a second-order prior may again be neutral. (2) Band confusion is the dominant error, and for pooled RMSE a mean decode improves only with more evidence or better calibration. A dip prior adds evidence only when the wrong band implies an implausible dip change. (3) The author's post-processing doses were fitted on the public leaderboard and ran opposite to local validation, so local gains from damping/drift ramps may be noise or misleading; the 3.4 ft LOWO-to-hidden gap shows local protocols can mislead. (4) Faults (jumps in TVT + Z, simulated in the 1st-place augmentation) break the dip-persistence prior, so the transition needs a small jump probability. (5) With an absolute score of ~8.35, the tracker as a standalone member is unlikely to help a 4.7-4.8 ft system.
notes: The preprint's main value is methodological: the 'displacement law' (hidden-side optima of regularisation sit where local validation calls them harmful), the local/public/private inversions, and the rule that proportional mechanisms fail boundedly while discrete ones fail unboundedly (consistent with our failed XY hump picking and learned gates). The pseudo-typewell weight w = n/(n+3) and the clip on GR residuals are cheap details worth copying into our typewell-calibration channel. The author notes that public solutions converged on a robust low-order polynomial in U = T + Z. The related identity TVT + Z - ANCC = const (A18) could anchor u exactly. The preprint calls the metric MAE while other writeups report RMSE; treat its numbers with caution.
